cards.front: Recall a key point about Camera Controls and Exposure
cards.back: The exposure triangle: aperture (f-stop), shutter speed and ISO work together — changing one affects the others.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Camera Controls and Exposure
cards.back: Aperture controls depth of field: wide aperture (f/1.8) = shallow DoF; narrow aperture (f/16) = deep DoF.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Camera Controls and Exposure
cards.back: Shutter speed controls motion: fast (1/1000s) freezes action; slow (1/15s) creates blur and sense of movement.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Camera Controls and Exposure
cards.back: ISO controls sensor sensitivity: low ISO (100) = clean image; high ISO (3200+) = noisy/grainy but usable in low light.

cards.front: What should you know about photography exam tips?
cards.back: Show your camera SETTINGS for every image (aperture, shutter speed, ISO). Demonstrate UNDERSTANDING of the exposure triangle — not just what each setting does, but how they interact. Explain the CREATIVE REASON for each technical choice.

Students often make mistakes with this topic. Wrong: Auto mode will give you the best exposure every time. Correct: Auto mode makes AVERAGE exposure decisions that may not suit your creative intention. Manual control lets you CHOOSE: shallow or deep depth of field? Frozen or blurred motion?
